title: Traffic Light Before Toggle — Publish AI Permission First
content:
Hi [Name],

This week, school leaders are being asked to **turn AI on** in tools students already open every period — while teachers return from training without a single page they can pin in the staff room.

Communities that have moved past panic describe the same pattern: AI belongs **after** the learner attempts the work — for feedback, examples, or review — not to replace thinking, drafting, or explain-back.

IT teams can often limit student-facing assistants inside workspace suites, yet academic councils still debate bans as if toggles were impossible. When policies remove every app that "contains AI," legitimate reading and translation supports get caught in the net — and teachers hesitate to help the very learners who need structure.

Edtech voices add a second warning: **high engagement scores are not mastery** when reward loops replace creation.

EduHexa helps principals publish a **traffic-light permission map**, align witnessed assessment, and communicate with parents before the next renewal cycle.

Would you like our one-page **AI Traffic Light** template for faculty and parents?

Reply YES and we will share it.
excerpt: Student AI switches stay on in everyday classroom tools while teachers leave training without a publishable stop/ask/go map — the calm fix is permission before platform renewal.
